purpose: NAPIC residential existing stock (S_total) and completions (C) for four-quadrant v1 tests 2 and 3, and forward-ledger entry 005 (F2 by-state delta*).
discipline: Every value is transcribed from an official NAPIC file. Nothing is interpolated, estimated, smoothed, or sourced from any republication. Missing = null. Derived values are flagged with basis='derived_ytd_difference' and carry the raw cumulative figures they were derived from.

However the companion ANNUAL NARRATIVE REPORT (Laporan Stok Harta Tanah, a separate PDF in the same archive) carries a fully bilingual Technical Notes chapter that names every section and every dwelling concept in Malay. The mappings below are transcribed from Laporan Stok Harta Tanah 2025, sections 2.1-2.6 and 5.2. An earlier version of this file stated that no Malay column mapping existed; that was wrong and is corrected here.

dwellingTypes_ms_en.source: Laporan Stok Harta Tanah 2025 section 5.2 (Jenis Harta Tanah / Property Types)
dwellingTypes_ms_en.note: The Jadual's 11 columns further subdivide 'teres' and 'berkembar' by storey count (single vs 2-3 storey) and split low-cost into house vs flat. Those subdivisions are printed in English only.

existing_stock.officialDefinition: Units issued with certificate of completion and compliance (CCC)/certificate of fitness (CF) or temporary certificate of fitness (TCF) prior to the review period, plus units completed and issued with CCC within the review period. Reported figures are accumulative totals from previous periods plus the review period. Includes adjustments for delayed data, change in category of use, and destroyed/rebuilt units.

completions.officialDefinition: Completion is the term used when building construction works are completed and a certificate of completion and compliance (CCC) is issued.

incoming_supply.officialDefinition: Units where physical construction works are in progress during the review period. Accumulative totals which include starts recorded in the review period plus units under construction.

under_construction.officialDefinition: Reported as a separate section only up to 2017Q1; discontinued thereafter (incoming supply = starts + under construction).

starts.officialDefinition: Commencement of foundation and footing works of low-rise buildings, or works below ground level including piling and foundation of high-rise buildings.

planned_supply.officialDefinition: Units that have building plan approvals but have yet to start construction. Accumulative totals from previous periods plus new planned supply in the review year. Adjusted for lapsed and revised approvals.

new_planned_supply.officialDefinition: Units that have obtained building plan approvals within the review period; non-accumulative.

ytdRegime.officialText: NAPIC Explanatory Note 3 (Reformatting of Report): "Prior to Q1 2016, reported figures on 'Completions', 'Starts' and 'New Planned Supply' are non-accumulative and indicated totals within the review period. Starting Q1 2016, the reported figures are accumulative totals which include units recorded in the previous quarter plus units in the current quarter of the same year."
ytdRegime.handling: For 2016Q1 onward the published Q2/Q3/Q4 figures are labelled 'Q1 - Qn YYYY' and are year-to-date. This file stores QUARTERLY flows: Qn = YTD(Qn) - YTD(Qn-1), with Q1 taken as published. Every derived value carries basis='derived_ytd_difference' plus the two cumulative figures used. Validation: no derived quarterly completion is negative in any of the 74 periods.

seriesBreaks.2016Q1: SERIES BREAK — service apartments recategorised OUT of residential into commercial property from Q1 2016 (NAPIC Explanatory Note 2). Type columns drop from 12 to 11; national existing stock falls 4,928,883 → 4,876,439 despite positive completions. Do NOT compute a growth rate across 2015Q4→2016Q1.
seriesBreaks.2017Q1: SERIES BREAK (restatement) — NAPIC: "Revised in Q1 2017 to include data on projects that have been completed and issued with CCC in the prior years but have only been captured in the current study period." National existing stock jumps +355,289 while reported completions were only 20,325. The jump is a backlog catch-up, NOT new construction. Do NOT treat 2017Q1 ΔS as a completions flow.

validation.rowSumCheck: For every state-period-section row parsed, the sum of the type columns was checked against the printed Total. 0 failures across all 74 periods x 17 regions x 7 sections.
validation.coverage: Complete. existing_stock, completions, starts, planned_supply, new_planned_supply: 74/74 periods x 17 regions, no gaps, no missing cells. incoming_supply: 73 periods (2008Q1-2026Q1). under_construction: 38 periods (2007Q4-2017Q1, discontinued by NAPIC thereafter).
validation.ytdDifferencing: 0 negative derived quarterly completions (a negative would indicate the YTD assumption is wrong).
validation.anchorsNotApplicable: The MHPI and overhang anchors supplied for this task come from the Property Market Status Tables (Jadual Status Pasaran Harta Tanah), a DIFFERENT publication. They cannot be used to validate this stock file. See docs/methodology/napic-stock-sourcing.md for the cross-publication note.
validation.internalConsistencyChecks: These three checks are PARSING-INTEGRITY checks (did we transcribe the file correctly). They say nothing about whether the four-quadrant SE identity holds. See seIdentityCheck below for that.

seIdentityCheck.test: four-quadrant SE identity dS_total = C - delta*S_total, which with delta >= 0 requires dS <= C
seIdentityCheck.result: FAILS, systematically and in one direction.
seIdentityCheck.evidence: dS - C is positive in 65 of 73 quarters (negative in 5, zero in 3). Excluding the two documented 2016Q1/2017Q1 breaks it is positive in 64 of 71. Annually 2018-2025 the gap runs +0.59% (2021) to +1.29% (2025) of end-of-year stock, every year, no reversals. Cumulative 2018-2025: dS 1,099,803 vs C 663,566, gap 436,237 units.
seIdentityCheck.notNoise: An earlier version of this file reported "median identity residual ~0.15%" as if it were symmetric noise. That figure was the median ABSOLUTE residual PER QUARTER and it concealed the sign. The residual is a systematic one-directional bias, not noise. The earlier characterisation was wrong and is retracted.
seIdentityCheck.decomposition: Not concentrated anywhere. By dwelling type the gap is 20-50% of dS in all 11 type columns. By state it is positive in all 16 states plus the national total, ranging 9.7% (W.P. Putrajaya) to 60.6% (Terengganu) of dS. By quarter-of-year all four quarters are positive on average (Q1 and Q3 larger).

hypothesesTested.single dwelling type / service-apartment: REJECTED - gap positive in all 11 type columns, 19.9% (Flat) to 49.4% (2-3 Storey Semi-Detach) of that column dS
hypothesesTested.single state or administrative artifact: REJECTED - gap positive in all 16 states, 9.7% (W.P. Putrajaya) to 60.6% (Terengganu) of state dS
hypothesesTested.one-off restatement like 2017Q1: REJECTED - gap positive in 64 of the 71 non-break quarters

residual largest where NAPIC survey cove.verdict: INDETERMINATE - underpowered, neither confirmed nor rejected
residual largest where NAPIC survey cove.method: Spearman (scipy) across the 16 states. x = high-rise share of 2025Q4 existing stock = (Low Cost Flat + Flat + Condominium/Apartment) / total. y = (dS - C) / dS cumulated over 2018-2025.
residual largest where NAPIC survey cove.reading: rho = -0.415 is in the direction the coverage hypothesis predicts (the less high-rise a state is, the larger its residual) but p = 0.110 at n = 16 does not clear conventional significance. It cannot carry the explanation on its own.
residual largest where NAPIC survey cove.correction: CORRECTION 2026-08-02. An earlier version reported +0.29 and marked this hypothesis REJECTED on the grounds that the sign was wrong. That value came from the same factor-of-2 Spearman bug; the correct coefficient is -0.415, i.e. the OPPOSITE sign. The hypothesis was never rejected on valid grounds. It is now recorded as indeterminate rather than rejected, and the documented-cause explanation below does not depend on it either way.

seIdentityCheck.documentedCause: NAPIC states the gap by construction. (a) The quarterly report Explanatory Note 1.1 says existing inventory "comprises of adjustments made due to: delayed data from previous review periods but received during the review period; change in category of use; destroyed/rebuilt". (b) Laporan Stok Harta Tanah 2025 sections 2.3 and 2.5 state the survey "has not reached a total population count" and list "an increase in coverage" as a standing adjustment reason. (c) Laporan section 10.0 Coverage limits the survey to within local authority areas, housing schemes, and outside-scheme buildings that obtained building plan approval. Existing stock therefore absorbs previously unrecorded pre-existing units, which are not completions. COMPLETIONS counts only units observed to receive CF/TCF inside the surveyed universe during the quarter.
seIdentityCheck.whatRemainsUnknown: NAPIC publishes no reconciliation of the adjustment channels, so the gap CANNOT be decomposed into delayed data vs coverage expansion vs change of use vs demolition. Any split would be invented. Reported as cause documented, magnitude per channel unknown.

method.quarterlyResidual: resid(p) = [S_total(p) - S_total(p-1)] - C(p), MALAYSIA row, over the 73 quarter-pairs from 2008Q1 to 2026Q1
method.annualResidual: resid(y) = [S_total(y Q4) - S_total(y-1 Q4)] - sum of the four quarterly C flows in y
method.annualPercent: residual expressed over END-of-year stock S_total(y Q4); using start-of-year instead shifts each figure by at most 0.04pp and changes nothing
method.typeDecomposition: same residual computed column by column on the 11 type columns, cumulated 2018-2025, expressed over that column dS
method.stateDecomposition: same residual per state, cumulated 2018-2025, expressed over that state dS
method.breaksExcluded: 2016Q1 and 2017Q1 are excluded only where explicitly stated; the 65-of-73 count includes them

derived.note: Derived from the published values above. No raw reported figure has been altered. Annual C = sum of the four quarterly completions flows; annual dS = S(Q4,y) - S(Q4,y-1); S = S(Q4,y).

twoMeasures.delta_star_C_over_S: v1.0 frozen formula for four-quadrant section 4 test 2. LOWER BOUND on true stock growth: it misses completions occurring outside the surveyed universe.
twoMeasures.stock_growth_dS_over_S: growth of RECORDED stock. UPPER BOUND on true physical supply growth: it includes book-keeping accretion (delayed data, coverage expansion, change of use) that is not new construction.
twoMeasures.guidance: True physical stock growth lies between the two. Report as a bracket, never either one alone as a point estimate.

rankingRobustness.question: Does the choice between delta_star_C_over_S and stock_growth_dS_over_S change the STATE RANKING that forward-ledger entry 005 (F2) scores on?

method.statistic: Spearman rank correlation, scipy.stats.spearmanr (average ranks for ties)
method.variableA: delta_star_C_over_S = (sum of the four quarterly completions flows in year y) / S_total(y Q4)
method.variableB: stock_growth_dS_over_S = (S_total(y Q4) - S_total(y-1 Q4)) / S_total(y Q4)
method.denominator: end-of-year stock, S_total(y Q4), for BOTH variables
method.universe: the 16 states and federal territories; the MALAYSIA aggregate row is EXCLUDED
method.years: 2018-2025, chosen to sit entirely after the 2016Q1 and 2017Q1 series breaks
method.ties: none occurred; scipy average-rank handling would apply if they did
method.reproduce: For each year build the two 16-vectors from derived.annual[year].byRegion (skip the MALAYSIA key) and call spearmanr(A, B).

rankingRobustness.sensitivityToDenominator: Using start-of-year stock S_total(y-1 Q4) as the denominator instead gives mean 0.720, range 0.550-0.862. The choice of denominator moves the result by about 0.01 and changes no conclusion.
rankingRobustness.interpretation: The two measures agree SUBSTANTIALLY but are NOT interchangeable. Mean rho 0.710, and one year (2020) falls to 0.550, below the 0.6 bar that forward-ledger uses to pass a ranking-type prediction. REVISED CONCLUSION: it is NOT safe to claim F2 is immune to the delta* definition. F2 should be scored under BOTH measures and reported as indeterminate if the two disagree on the pass/fail side of its -0.3 threshold. An earlier version of this file asserted the choice "does not affect F2"; that assertion rested on the buggy 0.855 and is withdrawn.
rankingRobustness.correction: CORRECTION 2026-08-02. An earlier version of this field reported mean 0.855 (range 0.775-0.919). That was produced by a hand-rolled Spearman implementation containing a factor-of-2 error: it divided the sum of squared rank differences by 2*n*(n^2-1)/6 instead of n*(n^2-1)/6, which halves the deviation term and pushes rho toward 1. The values below are recomputed with scipy.stats.spearmanr. The corrected mean is 0.710, not 0.855. The earlier figure is retracted.

f2GateCheck.method: For each of the 16 states, compute the measure annually for 2008-2025 and find the longest run of consecutive years at or above 3%. Denominator is end-of-year stock. Run must be >= 3 years.
f2GateCheck.result: Only 2 states qualify under EITHER measure: W.P. Putrajaya and Terengganu. Under C/S the windows are 2016-2021 and 2015-2017; under dS/S they are 2021-2024 and 2023-2025. n = 2 is too few for the Spearman test F2 specifies.
f2GateCheck.implication: This is a limitation of the frozen proposition, not of the data. The threshold is frozen and must not be changed to manufacture sample size. Record as "sample too small, not scoreable" at the scoring date.
